source_title: BitNet (microsoft/BitNet) — Official Inference Framework for 1-bit LLMs

concepts.label: 1.58-bit weight quantization
concepts.description: Each number (weight) inside the AI model is stored using only 1.58 bits — meaning every value is restricted to just -1, 0, or +1 — instead of the usual 16 or 32 bits.
concepts.why_innovative: This drastically shrinks model size and eliminates expensive multiply operations, making it possible to run large AI models on ordinary laptops and phones without specialized hardware.

concepts.label: lookup table kernel
concepts.description: Instead of doing math calculations on the fly, the system pre-computes all possible results and stores them in a table, then just looks up the answer when needed — like using a cheat sheet instead of solving every problem from scratch.
concepts.why_innovative: This replaces slow, energy-hungry multiply-accumulate operations with ultra-fast memory lookups, enabling the 2–6x speed gains and 70–82% energy savings reported on consumer CPUs.

concepts.label: lossless 1-bit cpu inference
concepts.description: Running a 1-bit AI model on a regular computer processor (CPU) — not a specialized AI chip — while producing exactly the same answers as the full-precision model, with no quality loss.
concepts.why_innovative: It breaks the assumption that large AI models require expensive GPUs or cloud servers, enabling a 100-billion-parameter model to run on a single consumer CPU at human reading speed.

concepts.label: embedding quantization
concepts.description: Compressing the part of the model that converts words into numbers (embeddings) from high precision down to a smaller format, reducing memory usage further.
concepts.why_innovative: This extends quantization savings to a previously untouched part of the model, squeezing out additional speed (1.15–2.1x extra) and memory reduction on top of weight quantization.

concepts.label: parallel tiled kernel
concepts.description: The math operations are split into small, configurable tiles and processed simultaneously across multiple CPU cores, similar to breaking a big puzzle into pieces and solving them all at once.
concepts.why_innovative: This hardware-aware parallelism delivers an extra 1.15–2.1x speedup on top of the already-fast 1-bit kernels, pushing consumer-hardware performance even closer to cloud-level AI.

concepts.label: bitnet b1.58 architecture
concepts.description: A large language model (an AI that reads and generates text) designed from the ground up so that all its internal multiplications are replaced by simple additions and subtractions using only the values -1, 0, and +1.
concepts.why_innovative: It proves that a model trained with near-binary weights can match the quality of full-precision models, fundamentally changing the cost and accessibility of deploying AI at scale.
